#256 round 1: BLOCK
Head: 695aae4a4033941c44dfead656ef070febf9fef9
Request: 01a1f20e-3420-72b1-b233-a0e246928839

R256-001 [P2] Audit guard outcomes, not cache warmth
Location: harness/scripts/cache-ttl-audit.py:216-221.

The committed audit labels cache-state mismatches as send-guard errors.
new_false_cold tests !new_warm, even when new_guard is clear because the seat
is small. new_silent_cold similarly suppresses allowed cold deliveries when
their estimated cache is cold. The old columns omit the size condition too.
This changes ordinary command results, not just report wording, and makes
the promised after-deploy guard audit misleading.

Independent aggregation of the saved 13,404 paired rows, corroborated by
performance's execution of the committed command over the same 9,402 decided
deliveries, gives:

Metric                                  Before       Replayed after
Guard allowed, actually cold                 970                  710
  of which large                            265                    5
Guard refused/warned, actually warm             4                   56
Large guard refusals                         124                  436

The advertised 785 -> 47 and 33 -> 221 are not the guard-outcome metrics.
Of 221 advertised new false-cold cases, 165 are small/clear, including every
one of the 38 table-based cases. There are also 663 clear/cold cases omitted
from the advertised new silent-cold total. The large-only 265 -> 5 remains
valid. Small cold sends are deliberately allowed by this guard; distinguish
that policy scope from failures to protect large seats.

Repair: derive old guard disposition using size plus idle, and derive new
guard metrics directly from new_guard. Keep cache-state disagreement as
separately named columns if useful. Include warnings even for unknown TTLs
in refused-or-warned/warm accounting. Correct the PR body and durable audit
summary accordingly. Add a focused CI regression for small clear/warm,
small clear/cold, large refused/warm and unknown warned cases. No new audit
framework or exhaustive fixture inventory is needed. The coder acknowledged
this defect and is waiting for this verdict before the repair.

Why warm large seats would be refused

There are 52 newly refused-but-actually-warm deliveries: 32 Copilot and
20 OMP, all with their own recorded/split-derived 300-second TTL. This is
not caused by the fallback table, a lost 30-minute GPT TTL, or proxy
subagents being assigned an hour.

The OMP cases have 5.64-8.92 minutes idle (median 7.54). The coder's raw
metadata investigation additionally reports that all 32 Copilot sends
were past the previous call's native cacheExpiresAt; previous call duration
was median 3.5 seconds, maximum 11 seconds, and all were still past five
minutes measured from completion. The next-call read share was median
0.997. The coder reports no intervening calls, including subagents.
Those additional raw-transcript measurements are the coder's evidence,
not an independent transcript rescan by this reviewer.

Interpretation: the recorded TTL/expiry is not proof of actual eviction;
these observed caches remained usable beyond it. Thus option (a) really
does add warm-seat refusals in normal use. It implements the packet's
chosen conservative brake correctly rather than demonstrating a bad TTL
source. The pending prime decision between Refuse and Warn must be made
with the corrected 4 -> 56 friction figure. No grace or policy change is
invented by this review.

Other requested checks

- TTL provenance: inspected the pinned Unisphere 0370cab source. Copilot
  reads the current main-chain model's modelCacheState checkpoint; Claude
  derives from native ephemeral_1h/5m splits; OMP derives from usage.cttl
  splits, leaving absent splits unknown. The SDK's ttl_bucket maps through
  CacheTtl::from_label; a native 30m is preserved.
- Fallback order is native/derived, then proxy, then CACHE_TTL_TABLE v1.
  The served model beats the bound model; OMP table rows require the
  github-copilot route. Proxy's main-chain rewrite is one hour; its
  conversation-subagent path remains five minutes and is not the seat's
  main-chain status. Native evidence still takes precedence.
- Wire v2 emits cacheTtlSeconds; missing data defaults to Fact::Unknown,
  so a v1 card's legacy cacheTtl is ignored without refusing the card.
  Current CLI/TS clients consume daemon-rendered sizeLines/sizeColumns,
  not a closed TTL enum or version discriminator. Compatibility is
  established by source inspection; no explicit v1 decoding test was
  added. Both roster golden consumers cover the new warning marker.
- Unknown TTL plus large and idle >5m warns until the existing >60m
  ceiling, where refusal is intentional. Small seats remain clear.
  Force still needs a nonempty reason, records its event before delivery
  and includes TTL/basis in the audit. FYIs and controls remain exempt.
- FYI flush/revive require positive non-table evidence via cache_known;
  GPT's native 30m now qualifies. Idle nudge accepts only Clear/Busy,
  so warning or cold results do not wake the seat.
- Neither fleet_report* nor docs/how/prompt-cache-cost.md was edited.
  The audit selects usage, timing, model, route, seat and activity metadata;
  it outputs no message bodies, credentials or account information. Its
  JSONL scan necessarily reads whole log lines to select usage records,
  so "metadata only" describes extracted/retained/output data, not a
  promise that the underlying transcript files contain no messages.

Cost and validation

No new daemon process launches, transcript/status reads, loops, timers or
polls. Existing status reads remain on the delivery path and may read
appended transcript bytes; F214 adds a bounded five-row in-memory lookup,
not an additional per-delivery transcript pass. Existing list/PA reads
clone descriptors instead of selected fields. The PA's 60s round and the
existing F209 cursor/miss caching remain unchanged.

Performance's committed-command receipt: 12.18s wall, 5.73 CPU-seconds,
175,128,576 bytes peak RSS, zero swaps. It scans three spine queries on a
2.482GB store, 93.60MB calls, and 182 Copilot logs totaling 3.475GB.
This is on-demand whole-window work, not a tick or a per-seat background
cost. No duplicate whole-fleet replay was run by this reviewer.
